friction.recovery_path: - Wrong site, parent, person or nested child: return 404/403 without disclosing existence and with no mutation/audit side effect. - Validation error: preserve safe input, associate each error with its field and keep the actor on the same authoritative record. - Stale/concurrent/replayed action: create at most one effect; show the current version and a reasoned retry/review path. - Background/integration failure: preserve a visible queued/failed state, stable source identity and authorised retry/reconciliation path. - Exact routed error text observed in the selected path includes: Cannot assign an alert in ; Cannot acknowledge an alert in ; Cannot close an alert in . - Mapped correction/recovery actions: `updateMeta`; each must preserve prior provenance and re-check authority/state.

findings.current_behavior: Every import creates a new batch without a provider batch identity or payload fingerprint. Reconciliation locks only the selected batch; the supplied bank transaction is neither locked nor reserved, and the journal replay lookup is scoped only to that batch. findings.actor_and_job: A Privacy processor verifies, assigns, completes, refuses or withdraws a data-subject request through one authoritative lifecycle.

findings.current_behavior: The generic PUT accepts any allowed enum status, including completed, rejected and withdrawn, and persists it directly. Dedicated verify, complete and refuse actions also write without a shared state guard, transaction or row lock. Terminal records can therefore reopen or race into status/provenance combinations that no command validly produced.

current_workflow.summary: Permissions exist, but assignment/edit and lifecycle commands are not separated by one locked transition aggregate.

findings.current_behavior: After a generic per-domain permission check, ordinary Remove deletes the private-storage object and soft-deletes the row. It does not lock and authorize the concrete parent, retain an immutable digest/original, capture reason or destruction authority, or append revocation evidence.

current_workflow.summary: Soft deletion hides the metadata after the binary has already been irreversibly removed.

findings.problem_root_cause: Evidence removal is modelled as ordinary CRUD under concern-update authority instead of an immutable evidence aggregate with append-only, independently approved revocation.
